headline: Europe holds steady after Wall Street's slide, but Fed-hike talk hits metals hard
tone: Mixed, leaning defensive: Europe's equities have held the line and Nvidia's beat has stopped the chip rout spreading, but the selling has moved into metals as a firmer dollar and talk of a December Fed hike raise the cost of holding them. Not a broad risk-off, but not a return of appetite either.
body: The overnight story partly held: Nvidia's beat kept Europe's chip and equipment names from following Tuesday's US slide, though its halt to H200 shipments to China (about $2.4 billion of Q3 sales) and the board's refusal to bring back Jensen Huang keep the AI trade on probation.

The sharpest selling is in metals. Gold, silver, copper and platinum are all lower, pinned by the dollar's strength and reports that traders are pricing a December Fed hike, not a cut; silver is at its lowest in over a year.

UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October from 3.5%, driven by motor fuel, with core steady at 2.8% and food inflation the lowest since 2021. Gilts are the one major bond market under pressure, and Cornwall Insight's forecast of a 26% jump in the January energy price cap points to more energy-led inflation to come.

Crude has slipped after industry data showed a 5.3 million barrel US stock build, which outweighs, for now, the Hormuz tanker risk. What would change the tone: a hawkish read in tonight's FOMC minutes would extend the dollar and metals moves, while a softer read would give Europe's equity resilience room to turn into a rally.

views.text: Europe's resilience after a sharp US sell-off says the damage was concentrated in US software and AI-leadership worries, not a global growth scare. The test at the US open is whether Nvidia's beat can lift chips without software dragging tech again.

A US crude stock build and weaker refining margins point to an oil market looking past Hormuz headlines for now. In gas, the January UK price-cap forecast is a reminder that low European storage still sets the winter floor even as prompt TTF eases.

findings.summary: UK CPI rose to 3.6% in October on fuel while core held at 2.8%, so the uptick looks energy-driven rather than broad; the January cap forecast suggests that pressure is not finished.

findings.summary: Metals are falling on reported December Fed-hike bets and a strong dollar; tonight's FOMC minutes are the test of whether that pricing is justified.
Nvidia is ending H200 shipments to China, removing a roughly $2.4 billion quarterly sales line; the beat lifts hardware sentiment but narrows the growth story.
